newsitem.title: USA: Mystery "mine" spotted off Florida Keys.
newsitem.headline: Mystery "mine" spotted off Florida Keys.

text.p: A U.S. Navy explosives team was dispatched to the usually serene Marquesas Keys east of Key West on Friday to investigate a mysterious floating device that closely resembled an explosive mine.

The barnacle-encrusted metal sphere was spotted on Thursday in the azure waters just southwest of the horseshoe-shaped chain of uninhabited islands, a popular spot for tourists on day trips from Key West.
The sighting raised fears that the object might be a dangerous device left from as long ago as the Second World War, possibly laid to protect the Florida coast from patrolling German submarines.
"It's very, very encrusted. Obviously it's been in the water for a long time," said Chief Petty Officer Karl Stahl, a spokesman for the Key West Naval Air Station.

But he said the object most likely was an unarmed device used by the Navy for mine practice, which could have drifted away during those manoeuvres. "From what we can gather right now it looks like a Mark 6 practice mine," he said.
Navy divers based in Mayport, Fla., were set to jump from a helicopter into the water to inspect and positively identify the object on Friday.
